Band: zero-width at the Redis/Memcached standard-support rate. The Valkey engine is CHEAPER and Extended Support is DEARER; both are different products/support states, not a price range for this row, so they are named here rather than used as band edges.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 12,000 req/s peak. Mix: 55% home timeline, 24% single tweet/profile, 15% media fetch, 4% engagement (like/retweet/follow), 2% post (~240 tweets/s peak)

assumptions.subject: fanout
assumptions.statement: HYBRID fanout: an average post is written into ~200 follower timelines at write time; accounts above ~100k followers are excluded and pulled at read time instead. A worker sustaining ~8,000 timeline cache writes/s therefore clears ~40 posts/s. The amplification is encoded in the worker's CAPACITY (40 rps/instance), not as a visit probability above 1, so the arrival numbers stay literal request counts

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Timeline cache hit-rate 88% on the home timeline and 65% on tweet/profile reads; misses fall through to the read replicas

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Cache instance count (2) is set for working-set MEMORY and HA, not rps: at ~10k rps it uses ~5% of its request capacity

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: CDN hit-rate 90% on media; ~150 KB average delivered object

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: The SQL primary is modelled as ONE instance because there is one writer. A Multi-AZ standby is assumed in a real deployment but is NOT modelled as a second instance: it serves no traffic, and the engine would credit it with capacity it does not have. The engine will therefore flag the primary as a single point of failure - that flag is correct about failover, not about capacity.

assumptions.subject: q
assumptions.statement: The fanout bus runs 3 brokers for quorum/HA, not for throughput: at ~240 msg/s it is ~0.3% loaded. That is the minimum honest HA shape, not over-provisioning

assumptions.subject: api
assumptions.statement: API tier ~2,000 rps/instance (timeline assembly from cache, JSON serialisation)

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Monthly usage volumes (egress/storage/requests) are derived from AVERAGE load = peak / 3; capacity and instance counts are sized to PEAK. A single system_rps cannot carry both, so the peak:average ratio is stated here rather than hidden in a volume.

assumptions.subject: pricing
assumptions.statement: Delivery egress is priced at the model's single flat internet-egress rate ($0.09/GB, the US first paid tier). At the petabyte-per-month volume this design implies, a real committed CDN contract is roughly 5-10x cheaper, so the egress line is an UPPER BOUND, not a quote. The volume (GB/month) is the engineering claim; the rate is not negotiated here.

assumptions.subject: scope
assumptions.statement: Search, trends, DMs, ads and the ML ranking pipeline are OUT of this reference. Adding ranking would put a feature store and a scorer on the home-timeline path and would very likely move the bottleneck

_library.summary: Read-dominated microblog where posting fans out into per-user timeline caches.
